text:
The Mammoth went into Wednesday without a win in six games (0-3-3) and came out of it with a 4-1 win over Colorado and, by the sound of it, a rivalry. "If you touch any of our top guys, me and the boys are coming for you," Liam O'Brien said, as quoted by the Denver Post's Corey Masisak. It was that kind of night: 22 penalty minutes for Colorado, 20 for Utah, and a violent first period that saw Martin Necas take a scary hit, per Yahoo Sports.

O'Brien, never drafted and on a 5% chance, opened the scoring early in the second, and the win chance jumped from 52% to 71% on that one shot. Vincent Trocheck made it 2-0 with a power-play slapper late in the period, and Dmitri Simashev added a shorthanded goal 62 seconds into the third. That was the game. Parker Kelly's deflection, a 2% look, broke the shutout; Kevin Stenlund's late goal restored the three-goal margin.

The process was closer than the score. Utah won expected goals (the quality of the chances) 3.91 to 2.29, but most of that gap came on special teams: at even strength Colorado led 1.66 to 1.14 and outshot Utah 31 to 29. Sebastian Cossa made 30 saves, 1.3 goals better than the shots deserved, and was the first star. At the other end, Mackenzie Blackwood made the biggest save of the night on Anders Lee, a 69% chance in the first.

For Colorado, this is the shape of the next month. Nathan MacKinnon is out about a month and Cale Makar about two weeks, per Field Level Media, and the depth that carried them past Montreal on Saturday went 0 for 4 on the power play here and won 21 of 67 faceoffs. If Necas is hurt too, the margin gets very thin.

These two unveiled their Winter Classic uniforms the same day. Wednesday gave that game a little more edge.
headline: Mammoth end the skid and find a rival
